effect: Glucagon is in the blood and travelling toward the liver, so I can follow its effect on the stored carbohydrate.

reason: This is the only available combination, and it follows the stated goal of obtaining stored glucose.
expectation: I expect glucagon to signal the liver to break down some stored carbohydrate and release glucose into the blood.

effect: The liver store released glucose into the blood, completing the between-meals example and showing that the release signal eases as blood glucose rises.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the earlier liver store put to use.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following glucagon to the liver was worthwhile because it connected stored carbohydrate to fuel available between meals.

leastWorthwhile.text: Releasing the two messages felt somewhat repetitive, although the different conditions made their purposes clear.

surprise.text: Insulin stayed outside the muscle cells while glucose became stored carbohydrate; the message was not the building material.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary: the goals and pictures explained where each message was going. The menu supplied the compatible pairings, though, so I did not discover them myself.

continue.text: I would probably continue for another chapter to see more connections between body systems, though the short, guided sequence left little room for decisions.
